title: The latest-move gate misreads a tarball-published release: no gitHead, bare npm view answer
description: Found by the 0.11.0 promote dry run, 2026-09-27, after opum-agent's go. It refused, and nothing moved. 0.11.0 was published from tarballs (QCLI-366), which records no gitHead. npm 12 then answers `npm view <pkg>@0.11.0 dist.integrity gitHead --json` with a bare ["sha512-..."], not [{field: value}], so the QCLI-388 reader read "npm serves nothing" for all seven packages and gitHead null: a uniform null from the reader, not the registry. Its only live probe had used 0.10.0, which carries a gitHead. Condition 3 as built (commit == npm gitHead) also could never pass for a tarball-published release. opum-agent ruled the fix with fail-closed constraints (OPAG-465): the commit comes from the v<version> tag, dereferenced explicitly through the annotated tag object; an unreadable tag refuses; a present gitHead must also agree; condition 4, the byte binding, is unchanged. Match lore-cli's reader where it is sound.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The reader reads the exact 0.11.0 registry shape (a whole-version view with no gitHead key) for all seven packages
Condition 3 takes the commit from the v<version> tag peeled through the tag object; a wrong peel, an unreadable tag and a disagreeing gitHead each refuse
A mutation reverting to gitHead-only reddens the tarball-published case while the gitHead-present case stays green
The live promote dry run for 0.11.0 passes against the real receipt and registry

finalSummary:
Ported lore-cli's reader shape (scripts/pair-receipt.mjs at lore main bb225f1c, read by API) into scripts/qualification/pair-receipt.mjs, as opum-agent ruled on OPAG-465.

How it works now:
- viewVersion reads each version's WHOLE metadata with `npm view <pkg>@<v> --json --prefer-online`, taking dist.integrity and gitHead by presence.
- resolveTagCommit reads refs/tags/v<v> exactly and follows git/tags/<sha> while the object is a tag, up to 8 levels, accepting only a commit. It fails closed on a 404, a ref mismatch, a malformed answer, a peel ending on a non-commit, or a chain too deep, with no branch fallback.
- Condition 3: pair.quest.commit must equal the tag peel, and a present gitHead must also agree. Condition 4, dist.integrity on all seven, is unchanged.

Verified, with the repo at quest 0.11.0 (package.json), bun 1.3.14, npm 12.1.0:
- 6 new tests use the exact shapes measured live: a one-element array holding a whole-version object with no gitHead key, and v0.11.0 as ref -> tag object 84cc917 -> commit eb1d9f4. They cover the clean pass, a wrong peel refused, a missing tag refused, a gitHead that agrees (pass) or disagrees (refused), a peel through the tag object (a receipt naming the tag sha refuses), and a cyclic peel failing closed.
- Mutation: reverting the commit source to gitHead-only turned exactly the predicted test red, the tarball-published clean case. The gitHead-present case stayed green.
- LIVE: `node scripts/promote-release.mjs --record ~/.quest-release/promotion-0.11.0.json` (dry run) now says "Pair receipt opum-ai/opum-cli-e2e@main:receipts/pair/0.11.0.json qualifies quest 0.11.0 with lore 0.11.0, and all 7 tarballs npm serves match it", exit 0. Before the fix, the same command refused, reading nothing for any package.
- bun run check exit 0, 779 tests.
